problems.description: Deletes the entire existing baseline (index.ts, Express/SQLite, -106 lines) and replaces the project with an unrelated static-site generator rather than extending or integrating with the existing codebase; package.json name shifts from the prior app to 'ssg', confirming a total replacement.
33 convention violations across cache.ts, cli.ts, dev-server.ts (camelCase classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions), yielding a convention score of 0.49.
Cognitive complexity +29 across the new files; nested conditional logic (e.g. tag parsing ternaries in loadPage) exceeds the baseline's complexity.
Mixed module system in cli.ts: ESM import/export syntax combined with a CommonJS `if (require.main === module)` entry guard.

New files declare no classes (+0) and rely on module-level functions only; combined with the PascalCase violations this suggests the agent did not establish a consistent codebase-wide naming/structure convention.

strengths: Clean layered structure: CLI entry (src/cli.ts) decoupled from core generator (src/generator.ts) via typed BuildOptions and Page interfaces.
Testing infrastructure added from the start (jest.config.js, ts-jest preset, test script).
No new bugs (+0), smells reduced (-3), and 0.0% duplication per SonarQube.
commit_reviews.summary: Builds a reasonably modular greenfield SSG skeleton with test infra, but earns a weak 0.55 architectural fit by deleting the existing codebase outright and 0.45 convention adherence on 33 naming violations — the visible diff looks cleaner than the measured 0.49 suggests, so the violations concentrate in the truncated cache.ts/dev-server.ts portions.

problems.description: Adds two competing template engines (Handlebars and EJS) in a single commit, doubling the template, partial-registration, and test surface; a single engine would fit the feature scope.
Cognitive complexity +29 for only 6 new functions, driven by nested try/catch and conditional branching in findTemplate and renderWithTemplates.
registerPartials registers every Handlebars partial under two names (bare and 'partials/' prefixed), a redundant behavior not justified by the code.
Two new runtime dependencies plus a type package for a templating feature; risk of unused-engine drift if only one engine is exercised in practice.

strengths: Extends the existing BuildOptions and CLI parseOptions patterns consistently rather than inventing a parallel config mechanism
Feature is well-factored into small single-purpose helpers (findTemplate, registerPartials, renderTemplate, renderWithTemplates)
Preserves existing async/parallel structure via Promise.all and mirrors the established path.resolve default conventions
Includes test coverage (test/generator.test.ts modified) for the new behavior
commit_reviews.summary: A well-factored, pattern-consistent template feature that fits the generator architecture, but ships two template engines at once and adds notable cognitive complexity; note the 0.49 convention score reflects pre-existing violations in untouched files (cache.ts, dev-server.ts) and pre-existing cli.ts issues rather than this diff.

problems.description: Mechanical convention score is 0.49 with 33 violations flagged across cli.ts, cache.ts, and dev-server.ts (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions).

Discrepancy: most flagged violations are in cache.ts and cli.ts pre-existing code NOT modified by this commit, and dev-server.ts contains no classes (only camelCase functions and already-PascalCase interfaces), so the 0.49 score over-penalizes this diff's actual additions.
SonarQube delta shows +1 smell and +5 cognitive complexity introduced; the stateful rebuild-chain in startDevServer (rebuild promise serialization + chokidar watchers) is the likely source.

strengths: Dev server reuses generator.buildSite and extends BuildOptions, staying consistent with the existing module architecture.
Path traversal guard in serveFile (path.resolve + prefix check, 403 response) shows good security awareness.
Clean lifecycle handling: watcher.close, client.terminate, and server.close all awaited in DevServer.close.
Port validation (integer 1-65535) and flag parsing follow the established parseOptions pattern.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured dev-server feature that reuses existing generator patterns and handles security/cleanup correctly, but the mechanical convention score of 0.49 is largely driven by pre-existing violations in files this commit never touches.

problems.description: Rebuild path calls `buildSite({ ...options, plugins: [] })`, silently disabling ALL plugins during watch-triggered rebuilds — the dev server's rebuild behavior diverges from its initial build, and any user-registered plugin is dropped on change.

A `DevServerPlugin` instance is pushed into `plugins: PluginConfig[]`, mixing live plugin instances with config objects in one array; plugin lifecycle/instantiation semantics are inconsistent with the typed signature.
Cognitive complexity +25: `DevServerPlugin.onStart` packs server setup, WS upgrade handling, watcher, and shutdown into a single nested-callback method.
generator.ts collapses `PageMetadata`/`Page`/`BuildOptions` onto single lines, trading readability for diff compactness.

strengths: Public `startDevServer` API is preserved as a thin wrapper, keeping the change backward-compatible.
Rendering concerns (markdown/template) extracted into plugins, decoupling the generator from gray-matter, marked, handlebars, and ejs.
Net reduction of 215 lines, -1 smell, 0 new bugs, 0.0% duplication.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid plugin-architecture refactor that reduces coupling and preserves the public API, but it carries real debt via the rebuild path disabling all plugins, an instance-vs-config type mismatch in the plugins array, and a +25 cognitive complexity spike in DevServerPlugin.onStart.

problems.description: Cache key only covers source + template hashes; changes to plugin code (markdown/template) or plugin options in configFile do not invalidate .ssg-cache.json, so an incremental build can emit stale HTML from cached html with a v1 manifest that is blind to plugin version.
Module-level mutable lastBuildStats singleton couples CLI output to process-global state; it survives --clean rebuilds and is not reset, so stats can describe a prior run.
context.cache.parsed is populated from the previous manifest but the cache-hit path reads previous.pages directly; the parsed map is unused scaffolding in the visible diff unless consumed by plugins.
The diff ships no tests for the new incremental/caching behavior despite the feature's correctness sensitivity (story sessions otherwise require jest tests).

Discrepancy: measured convention score 0.49 lists violations like 'Classes should use PascalCase' in cache.ts and 'Functions should not use snake_case' in cli.ts that do not match this diff — no classes are added and added functions are camelCase; violations also cite dev-server.ts which this commit never touches, indicating a whole-file/absence-based checker artifact rather than violations introduced here.

strengths: Hashing utilities cleanly isolated in a new cohesive src/cache.ts module.
Integrates with existing architecture: cache flows through context.emitFile and the plugin pipeline, and BuildOptions/cli parsing follow the established pattern.
Opt-in --incremental/--clean flags and updated usage string keep the CLI backward compatible.
TypeScript-strict idioms maintained: explicit return types, interfaces over type aliases, node: prefixed imports, no any.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid cross-cutting incremental-build feature that fits the generator's plugin architecture and is backward compatible, but it accrues debt via a plugin-blind cache key and process-global stats — and its 0.49 convention score is dominated by checker artifacts, not conventions this diff actually breaks.

compounding_issues: Seed codebase (Express Todo API) was entirely unrelated to the SSG story; Session 1 discarded it wholesale, so the greenfield session had zero continuity with the seed
Dual template engines (Handlebars + EJS) committed in Session 2 became a permanent complexity surface that Sessions 4-5 had to carry through partials, layouts, and fallback rendering

DevServerPlugin.rebuildSite hardcodes plugins:[] on live-reload rebuilds, silently dropping user plugins during 'serve' while honoring them in 'build' — a latent build/serve behavioral split introduced by the Session 4 refactor

test/cli.test.ts was never updated after serve/--incremental/--clean were added; it still only passes because Jest substring-matches the unchanged 'Usage: ssg build' prefix, leaving the new CLI surface untested
key_decisions: Session 1: clean greenfield split of CLI (src/cli.ts) from build core (src/generator.ts) with recursive frontmatter Markdown discovery and a clean-output rebuild strategy
Session 2: dual-engine template support (Handlebars + EJS) with layout/partial conventions and a built-in HTML fallback when no template is specified
Session 3: standalone dev server with WebSocket live-reload, chokidar watching of content+templates, and static path-traversal protection, wired in as a CLI subcommand

Session 4: the architectural pivot — plugin system with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd lifecycle hooks, TS config/plugin loading via a require.extensions transpiler, Markdown/Template extracted into plugins, and the dev server converted into DevServerPlugin
Session 5: incremental builds via a SHA-256 content-hash manifest (.ssg-cache.json) with template-hash invalidation and full-rebuild fallback, exposing cache state on the plugin context
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 establishes a clean, minimal core; Session 2 adds features (templates, layouts, partials) in a well-scoped way; Session 3 delivers a genuinely polished dev server with live reload and traversal protection. Session 4 is the pivotal refactor that reorganizes the accumulating feature set into a plugin architecture instead of letting it accrete in one file — a decision that pays off in Session 5, where incremental caching slots directly into the plugin pipeline. The generator core shrank from a monolithic 108-line build to a composable pipeline, test coverage grew from 2 to 7 tests tracking every major feature (template rendering, plugin ordering, cache invalidation), and all sessions exited successfully with no error cascades.
story_review.summary: A textbook incremental-build story: each session composes on the last, the Session 4 refactor keeps architecture from accreting, and Session 5's caching leverages the plugin design — overall coherence is very high with only minor compounding debt (unrelated seed, dual template engines, untested CLI surface).
